clue.text: Japanese extract of borage is harmful

indicators.note: extract of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A herbalist warns that a preparation made from borage can do harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extract of' sounds like herbal medicine, but it signals letters taken from inside 'borage is harmful': boraGE IS HArmful.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a traditional female entertainer of Japan, so the adjective here stands as a noun for a Japanese person.

clue.text: Speak fast

explanation.surface: An instruction to talk quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a view is to voice or speak it; an express train or delivery is a fast one.

clue.text: Yen to follow road and cross river

indicators.note: the yen piece is set after the road piece, following it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone longs to walk along a road and then get over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts Y after ST; the clue's 'and cross river' reads as a journey, but 'cross' gives X and 'river' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Styx is the river of the underworld the dead must be ferried over.

clue.text: Repay debt, out of a hole

parts.note: a mortise is a hole or slot cut in timber to take a tenon in joinery

explanation.surface: Paying off what you owe gets you out of a financial hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of a hole' reads as escaping money trouble, but here 'out of' means 'made from': the answer is built from A plus a carpenter's hole, MORTISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise a loan is to pay it off gradually in instalments.

clue.text: Killer whale following ship turned from side to side

indicators.note: turned says the whole run of letters built so far is read backwards
the whale piece is placed after the ship piece

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the orca is the killer whale

explanation.surface: A killer whale swims behind a ship that then swings about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the whole string, not just the whale; 'following' sets the whale after the ship before the turn. 'from side to side' is the definition, not part of the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Across means extending from one side to the other, as a bridge runs across a river.

clue.text: It's blown up by accident

parts.note: reads as something destroyed by mistake, but means a car safety cushion that inflates when a crash happens

explanation.definitionFit: A car's safety cushion inflates automatically in a collision, so it is inflated because of a crash.

clue.text: Study unknown cheese picked up off the shelf

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
Y is an unknown in algebra

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the cheese is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A student reaches for a mystery cheese taken from the supermarket shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like lifting the cheese, but in a down clue it turns EDAM into MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ready-made is produced in advance and sold as is, which is what buying off the shelf means.

clue.text: Fronting the main marine guard

parts.note: marine means of the sea
to ward is to guard, as in ward off

explanation.surface: A naval sentry stands at the front of the main deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the poetic name for the open sea, so 'Fronting the main' means facing the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaward describes facing or moving toward the ocean, the old 'main'.

clue.text: Tipsy occasion, when drinks are cheap

parts.note: happy is a mild word for slightly drunk
an hour can mean a particular time or occasion, as in 'the hour has come'

explanation.surface: A night out where people get merry because the bar has cut its prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars run a set period of discounted prices early in the evening to bring in customers.

clue.text: Fame! Hope it's around for ages

indicators.note: around means the letters of the words are spun about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan hopes the musical Fame will have a very long run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal; 'for' is a link, and 'Fame!' looks like the musical's title but is plain fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Having ages means having plenty of time, a long while to spare.

clue.text: Help! One's trapped by overturned rock

indicators.note: trapped by says the numeral goes inside the turned rock
overturned means the rock word is read backwards

parts.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cry for help from someone pinned beneath a rock that has toppled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns LAVA into AVAL, and 'trapped by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in 'to no avail', meaning without help.

clue.text: Ex-president's said to be at home in society of lawyers

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was a former US president

indicators.note: said means the last piece is the spelling of a word that sounds the same as the one meant

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A former president is supposedly a member of a legal society.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln's Inn is one of the four Inns of Court in London to which every barrister in England and Wales belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inns of Court are professional bodies of barristers, so this Inn is a society of lawyers.

clue.text: It indicates presence of American border

parts.note: a hem is the edged border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A sign shows the presence of the US frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the small cough people give to announce they are in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A throat-clearing noise is made to draw attention, signalling that the speaker is there.

clue.text: Careful with shower -it keeps dripping

parts.note: steady means careful and controlled
a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: Advice to go gently with a leaky shower that will not stop dripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent wet weather falls continuously, which is to keep dripping.

clue.text: It can be killing to be kept in this

definitions.text: It can be killing to be kept in this

parts.words: It can be killing to be kept in this
parts.note: reads as a cell or prison, but means the nervous state of waiting which we call 'killing' when it is unbearable

explanation.definitionFit: Being kept waiting in uncertainty is said to be killing you, as in 'the wait is killing me'.

clue.text: Look: new kid almost dotty

parts.note: ecce is Latin for behold, look

indicators.note: almost means the trick word loses its final letter

parts.note: to kid is to trick or hoax

explanation.surface: Look at the new child: he seems slightly mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to fool; 'almost' cuts TRICK to TRIC. ECCE, Latin 'behold', is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric and dotty both describe someone odd or slightly unhinged.

clue.text: Sound made by car coming to roundabout

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker
O is round in shape, like a roundabout

explanation.surface: Noise from a car arriving at a traffic circle.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundabout is the British name for a traffic circle; its round shape gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio means relating to sound and its recording.

clue.text: Three characters from Glyndebourne opera performing for one at theatre

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are acted out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the first three letters of Glyndebourne

explanation.surface: Members of a Glyndebourne opera production put on a show for a single theatre visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Glyndebourne is an English country-house opera festival. 'performing' rearranges GLY with OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A playgoer is someone who attends the theatre.

clue.text: Foreign money poured into football club

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ran means poured or flowed, as a liquid does

explanation.surface: Overseas cash has been pumped into a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poured into' reads as investment in a club, but 'poured' is a past tense meaning flowed and 'into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and remains that of Switzerland.

clue.text: Lover's married, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A suitor has sadly turned out to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' signals rearranging MARRIED; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone who is romantically attracted to another, a suitor.

clue.text: Russia in claim against navy: it makes you sick

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the navy letter is set beside the rest
in places the Russia letter inside the claim word

parts.note: to allege is to claim
R is used for Russia

explanation.surface: Russia lodges a legal claim against a foreign navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside ALLEGE to make ALLERGE, and 'against' sets N beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergen is a substance such as pollen that triggers an allergic reaction.

clue.text: Commons division — let me through!

explanation.surface: An MP calls for a vote and pushes through the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons a gangway is the aisle dividing the benches; 'Gangway!' is also the shout to clear a path.
explanation.definitionFit: The aisle splitting the Commons benches is so named, and the same word is shouted to make people stand aside.

clue.text: They fly in European newspaper for a schilling

indicators.note: for means the newspaper letters replace the schilling letter

parts.note: a Swiss person is a European
S is the abbreviation for the Austrian schilling
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Birds appear in a European paper that once cost a schilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals swapping: FT replaces one S in SWISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Swifts are fast birds that spend almost their whole lives on the wing.

clue.text: Kinky sin? May yawn quite a bit

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Kinky sins may leave someone yawning with boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' signals rearranging SIN, MAY and YAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is true in many respects means it is so to a considerable degree.

clue.text: Rant, stir hearts in opposition

indicators.note: hearts are the central parts, so take the middle letters of each word

explanation.surface: A protester rants and stirs up feelings against the regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' takes the middles of RANT and STIR: AN and TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means against, being opposed to something.

clue.text: Eat up, girl!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A parent tells a daughter to finish her food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat up' reads as a command to finish dinner, but 'up' turns DINE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, used in crosswords for any girl.

clue.text: Stray starts to 'oller — real howler

parts.note: to err is to stray from what is right

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch 'holler' from someone straying into a real blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oller is 'holler' with the H dropped, a shout. 'starts to' takes the O and R that begin 'oller and real.
explanation.definitionFit: A howler is a glaring mistake.

clue.text: Ever after, silly frown on Mo

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are mixed up foolishly

explanation.surface: Someone gives a girl called Mo a silly scowl forever after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges FROWN, ON and MO.
explanation.definitionFit: From now on means henceforth, for all time after this moment.

clue.text: Uproar: Father joins mediation group

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
ACAS is the UK Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which mediates industrial disputes

explanation.surface: A priest joins the conciliation service during a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is a British public body that mediates between employers and unions.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or brawl.

clue.text: Embarrassed to look at boob in photo

parts.note: red describes a face flushed with embarrassment
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone blushes on seeing an unflattering photograph of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boob' means a blunder, not anatomy: the photographic flaw where a flash makes pupils glow.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye is a common mistake in flash photography where eyes appear glowing red.
